title: Add option to save files in current working directory
description:
Note that this is somewhat less than useful when run from
the Finder on macOS (returns the root directory) or from
a shortcut (including the taskbar) on Windows (returns whatever
is set as the fixed "run in" directory for the shortcut, which
is usually the directory where the program resides, certainly
for the shortcut the installer sets up.)

We could try to do the same kind of workaround as done in
get_persdatafile_dir() and for the other file open style settings.
OTOH, this isn't the default setting (as platform UI guidelines
recommend against this sort of thing on macOS and Windows), so
perhaps caveat emptor is ok here.

Fix #1237

notes.body:
added 16 commits
  • 5e4c1167...2d6056c8 - 15 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 1b42370f - Add option to save files in current working directory
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16780/diffs?diff_id=1089018618&start_sha=5e4c116714083936f5fabb14317bc00baf4d098e)

> Note that this is somewhat less than useful when run from the Finder on macOS ... or from a shortcut (including the taskbar) on Windows ...

And probably not all that useful when launched from the GNOME or KDE or Xfce or... GUIs, either.  Maybe it's the user's home directory, maybe it's something else.

> so perhaps caveat emptor is ok here.

If it's the root directory, you probably won't be able to save there if you don't run Wireshark as root (_**you should not run Wireshark as root!**_), and, in newer versions of macOS, you won't even be able to save there if you *do* run it as root

```
$ sudo sudo sh -c 'echo Hello >/Hello'
-bash: /Hello: Read-only file system
$ mount | head -1
/dev/disk1s1s1 on / (apfs, sealed, local, read-only, journaled)
```

(macOS Ventura).

If it's the Wireshark installation directory, you probably won't be able to saver there unless *maybe* if you run Wireshark as Administrator (_**you should not run Wireshark as Administrator!**_).

So I think *caveat emptor* is fine.

In the best of all possible worlds, it would be possible, on all platforms, to determine whether the program was launched from a command line or not.

Good luck with that.  (For example, at least on UN\*Xes, "launched from a shell" does not guarantee "launched from a command line" - what if some file manager runs executables with `system()`?  It probably *shouldn't, but....)
